title: Even Minkowski uniqueness as a consequence of logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski
seo_title: Even Minkowski uniqueness and logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski | Alec Kriebel
meta_description: Two distinct uniqueness consequences: smooth positive even data for 0≤p<1, and arbitrary origin-symmetric bodies with equal unnormalized Lp measures for 0<p<1.
host_edition_qualification: Zenodo display edition only; not an author-supplied API version
abstract: We record consequences of OpenAI's recently released origin-symmetric logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski inequality. For every ambient dimension n ≥ 2 and 0 ≤ p < 1, every smooth strictly positive even density on Sⁿ⁻¹ has exactly one smooth positive even support-function solution of h¹⁻ᵖ det(∇²h+hI)=f, with positive curvature-radius matrix. For 0 < p < 1, identical Lₚ surface-area measures determine arbitrary full-dimensional origin-symmetric convex bodies. We give the nonsmooth first-variation and strictness argument explicitly and a local version of the smooth endpoint transfer of He–Liu. Existence and regularity are established inputs. These are consequences of the new inequality and known reductions, not a new proof of logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski or a claim of first public announcement. Equal-volume boxes exclude arbitrary-measure uniqueness at p=0.
